meta.title: Word Sets in Our Word Book
meta.textType: a new word from a word set

paragraphs: Posted by Lily. The Explorers have a word book, and we keep our words in sets. A set is a group of words about one topic. This week, we added new words to two sets. Mia drew a small picture next to each word.

The first set has the words for ways to cook. Chef Lucy showed us three of them in the cooking class. When you boil food, you cook it in hot water with bubbles. Rice and eggs are boiled in this way. When you fry food, you cook it in hot oil in a pan. When you bake food, you cook it in an oven, and a cake is a good example.

The new word in this set is roast. When you roast food, you cook it in an oven with a little oil. The outside of the food becomes brown, and the inside stays soft. We usually roast chicken and vegetables, but we bake bread and cakes. Leo added one more word, which is grilled. Grilled fish is cooked over a fire, and it has dark lines on the skin. Leo drew a picture of grilled fish next to the word. He is very good at drawing food.

The second set has the words for things to wear. It has the words shirt, shorts, socks, hat, and sneakers. The new word in this set is boot. A boot is a strong shoe that covers your foot and part of your leg. People wear boots in the mud or in the rain. I wear mine when we walk in the park. Another new word is kit. A kit is the set of clothes that you wear for a sport. A football kit has a shirt, shorts, and long socks. Tom has a green kit, and Ben has a red one.

Teacher Kim added a third small set for things that people wear on the body. It has the words watch, ring, and necklace. The new word is earring. An earring is a small thing that a person wears on the ear. I do not wear one, but my friend does. Teacher Kim says that we must not wear an earring on a trip or in sport.
Which set do you like best? Each new word has a place in the right set, and it is easy to find. Please add your own words to our word book.
text.summary: Lily writes about the word sets in the Explorers' word book. A set of cooking words gets two new words, roast and grilled, and a set of clothes words gets boot, kit, and earring.
